data.description: The project accepts Solidity compiler versions allowed by '^0.8.20', including releases that Slither flags for known compiler issues.
data.meaning: The project allows a Solidity compiler version that Slither associates with known compiler bugs.
data.next: Check the exact compiler version used by Foundry, compare it with the Solidity bug list, and pin a patched version that is compatible with the project.
data.title: Compiler version
data.why: A compiler bug can change how otherwise-correct Solidity behaves after compilation. This is a build-safety issue, not proof that the contract is exploitable.

data.description: The function release() makes a raw external call that can execute code in the receiving address.
data.meaning: The contract sends a call directly to another address instead of using a higher-level typed call.
data.next: Inspect the full calling function and trace the state changes before and after the call. Then reproduce the path with a hostile recipient in a Foundry test.
data.title: Low-level external call
data.why: The callee can control how that call behaves. Review reentrancy, return-value handling, recipient control, and whether state is updated safely around the call.

data.description: The enum 'status' uses a naming style that does not match the project's expected Solidity convention.
data.meaning: A Solidity identifier does not follow the naming convention configured or expected by Slither.
data.next: Rename it only if the project's style guide requires it. Do not treat this finding as a vulnerability.
data.title: Naming convention
data.why: This is primarily a readability and maintainability issue. It normally has no direct security impact.
